title: International Markets and Auctions
quiz.0.question: What is the largest single export market for Italian wine?
quiz.0.explanation: The US is Italian wine's largest export market, accounting for about a quarter of Italy's wine export value; Pinot Grigio, Prosecco and Barolo all enjoy very high brand recognition there.
quiz.1.question: In which cities are the main international fine-wine auctions held?
quiz.1.explanation: Christie's and Sotheby's hold their main wine auctions in London and New York, while Hart Davis Hart is based in Chicago. These three cities form the main market through which top Italian wines circulate.
quiz.2.question: What does the Liv-ex Fine Wine 100 index mainly track?
quiz.2.options.1: Market trading prices of top fine wines
quiz.2.explanation: The Liv-ex Fine Wine 100 is the main price index of the global fine-wine market, tracking trading prices of 100 top wines (including Italian Barolo and Brunello), and an important tool for watching market trends.
quiz.3.question: Which Italian wines have grown fastest in Asian markets in recent years?
quiz.3.options.1: Top DOCGs such as Barolo and Brunello
quiz.3.explanation: With growing numbers of high-net-worth consumers (HNWIs) in Asia, demand for top DOCGs such as Barolo and Brunello has grown clearly in Hong Kong, Singapore and mainland China, making them key lots in Asian auctions.
quiz.4.question: What do Wine-Searcher and Vivino mainly offer collectors of Italian wine?
quiz.4.options.0: The only platforms for subscribing to futures online
quiz.4.options.1: Global average market prices and historical price trends, as data for buying and selling decisions
quiz.4.options.2: Only useful for ordinary consumers choosing restaurant wines, not for collectors
quiz.4.options.3: Second-hand trading platforms that replace auction houses
quiz.4.explanation: Wine-Searcher aggregates prices from a huge number of retailers worldwide, showing the global price distribution and historical price curve for a specific wine; Vivino provides user ratings, market trends and stock distribution. Together they are free data tools for collectors to judge market value.
quiz.5.question: What is distinctive about Taiwanese consumers' preferences for Italian wine?
quiz.5.options.0: A preference for cheap Prosecco and everyday Pinot Grigio
quiz.5.options.1: A preference for age-worthy wines such as Barolo, Brunello and Amarone, with enthusiasts collecting mainly to learn
quiz.5.options.2: Only organic and natural wines, rejecting traditional oaked wines
quiz.5.options.3: A preference for rich southern reds, ignoring northern DOCGs
quiz.5.explanation: Taiwan's Italian wine market is driven mainly by well-informed enthusiasts; wine education such as WSET is widespread, consumers strongly prefer age-worthy top wines such as Barolo, Brunello and Amarone, and they study and collect systematically — one of the few Asian markets driven mainly by "knowledge-based buying".
quiz.6.question: What is the main advantage of a bonded warehouse for wine collectors?
quiz.6.options.0: Free, unlimited storage for all wines
quiz.6.options.1: Duty and VAT can be deferred when wine is resold in bond, lowering cross-border costs
quiz.6.options.2: Only auction houses can use bonded warehouses, not individuals
quiz.6.options.3: Wine stored in bond automatically carries a 100% authenticity guarantee
quiz.6.explanation: A bonded warehouse is a professional store where goods are held before import duty and VAT are paid. Wine traded in bond can change hands without leaving the warehouse, deferring tax obligations and greatly lowering the cost of cross-border trade — standard practice for top-wine collectors.
slides.0.title: International Markets and Auctions
slides.0.subtitle: How top Italian wine circulates worldwide, how auctions work and where the market is heading
slides.1.title: The Global Market for Italian Wine
slides.1.content:
Italy is one of the world's largest wine exporters, with annual exports of more than €7 billion. From everyday wines to top DOCGs, Italian wine reaches every level of the global market, and its top wines are important lots at international auction houses.

US market: Italy's largest export market, with Pinot Grigio and Prosecco for the mass market and Barolo / Brunello for the fine-wine market
European market: led by Germany, the UK and Switzerland, with a well-developed network of London fine-wine merchants
Asian market: Hong Kong became an auction hub after abolishing wine import duty in 2008, and Singapore is also a regional centre
slides.2.title: Three Leading International Wine Auction Houses
slides.2.content:
Christie's Wine — Founded 1766

Headquarters: London, New York | Holds wine auctions in several cities every year
Italian strengths: old Barolo vintages (1970-1990), Brunello di Montalcino Riserva, top Amarone
Services: expert pre-sale valuation, strict provenance checks, an emphasis on original wooden cases (OWC)

Sotheby's Wine — Founded 1744

Headquarters: London, New York, Hong Kong | One of the world's largest wine auctioneers
Italian strengths: Super Tuscans (Sassicaia, Ornellaia), the Gaja range, Soldera Brunello
Asian presence: the Hong Kong office serves Asian collectors locally, with Chinese-language catalogues and valuations

Hart Davis Hart — America's Top Wine Auctioneer

Headquarters: Chicago | Focused on fine-wine auctions for the US market
Italian strengths: Giacomo Conterno, Quintarelli Amarone, Biondi-Santi verticals
Known for: rigorous inspection of lots and detailed catalogues
slides.3.title: Key Markets: Asia vs North America
slides.3.content:
Asian Market (Hong Kong, Singapore, China)

Market size: after abolishing wine import duty in 2008, Hong Kong became Asia's most important wine-auction hub, with Sotheby's, Christie's and others holding wine sales there

Preferences: high-net-worth individuals (HNWIs) favour top DOCGs, verticals and internationally famous wines; brand recognition (Gaja, Sassicaia) is often as influential as scores

Growth drivers: a rising middle class, the spread of Western dining and wine education are driving demand for top wines such as Barolo / Brunello

Challenges: authentication (counterfeit top wines), poor storage conditions (hot, humid climate), changing tariff policies

North American Market (US, Canada)

Market size: the US is Italy's largest wine export market, worth about a quarter of export value; New York, California and Chicago are the main fine-wine markets

Preferences: American critics (Wine Advocate, Wine Spectator, Vinous) are highly influential and high scores clearly lift demand; Super Tuscans (Sassicaia, Tignanello) enjoy strong brand recognition

Growth drivers: the cultural identity of Italian-American communities, the popularity of Italian restaurants, wine education (WSET / CMS)

Challenges: alcohol laws differ by state and direct shipping to some states is still restricted; the multi-tier distribution system affects availability
slides.4.title: Asia-Pacific in Depth: Taiwan, Japan and Southeast Asia
slides.4.content:
Beyond the two hubs of Hong Kong and Singapore, Taiwan, Japan and Southeast Asia's emerging markets each have their own character and are important growth areas for Italian wine.

🇹🇼 Taiwan

  • Size: Italy is one of Taiwan's important sources of imported wine, with an active community of enthusiasts
  • Preferences: wine education such as WSET is widespread, and consumers know Barolo, Brunello and Amarone in depth, collecting mainly to learn
  • Opportunities: a well-educated, stable middle-class wine-drinking public with strong interest in visiting estates (wine tourism) and direct imports
  • Challenges: some top wines are monopolised by importers, and consumers have few channels to buy direct from estates

🇯🇵 Japan

  • Size: Tokyo is one of the cities with the most Michelin-starred restaurants in the world, and its sommeliers are among the very best
  • Preferences: Japanese consumers' emphasis on food pairing makes them natural partners for Italian wine; they favour elegant whites (Soave, Friulano) and refined reds (Barolo, Amarone)
  • Opportunities: Italian estates entering Japan and creative pairings with Japanese cuisine (washoku) attract much media and consumer attention
  • Challenges: French wine culture is deeply rooted, so Italian wine needs continued promotion through sommelier education

🌏 Emerging Southeast Asian Markets

Thailand: Bangkok's fine-dining scene is growing fast and the imported-wine market keeps expanding; preferences lean to Pinot Grigio, Prosecco and good-value Chianti Classico
Vietnam: a rising affluent middle class and fast-growing fine-wine merchants in Ho Chi Minh City; the French colonial legacy favours French wine, but Italian wine is catching up quickly on value and brand recognition
Indonesia / Philippines: the main market is high-end hotels and corporate entertaining; recognisable top wines such as Barolo and Brunello are the first choice as business gifts
slides.5.title: Digital Wine Market Platforms: A Collector's Toolkit
slides.5.content:
Digital platforms have changed price transparency and the way top wines are traded, and are essential information tools for today's collectors.

📊 Wine-Searcher

The world's largest wine price-comparison platform

Features: aggregates prices from a huge number of retailers worldwide, shows the global average and lowest price for any wine, historical price charts (Pro version) and where stock is located. For collectors: judge a reasonable buying price for a specific wine, compare prices between regions, and monitor the market value of your own cellar.

🍷 Vivino

The world's largest wine app community

Features: rating data from tens of millions of users, instant label scanning, market-popularity tracking, and the Vivino Market for buying and selling. For collectors: track public rating trends for specific wines and discover high-rated, still little-known niche wines.

📈 Liv-ex

The global professional exchange for fine wine

Features: tracking of indices such as the Fine Wine 100, B2B trading in bond, real-time market data and transaction records. For collectors: an institutional trading platform (individuals access it through member merchants) and an important tool for watching overall fine-wine market trends — though past performance does not predict the future.

🔨 Online Auction Platforms

Winebid, Acker, Zachys Wine Auctions

Winebid: a large American online wine auction platform holding weekly sales, with active trading in Barolo / Brunello — an efficient route for individuals to buy and sell Italian wine. Acker Merrall & Condit: a long-established New York auction house strong in Italian cult wines (Dal Forno, Quintarelli). Zachys: based in New York and Hong Kong, with active trading in Super Tuscans and Brunello.
slides.6.title: Auctions in Practice: Buyers vs Sellers
slides.6.content:
Whether buying a precious vintage at auction or consigning wines from your cellar, knowing how auction houses work is key to protecting your interests.

For Buyers

  • Buyer's premium: a buyer's premium (its rate depending on the auction house) is added to the hammer price and must be counted in the total cost
  • Provenance checks: check the provenance documents and ask the auction house for the storage history
  • OWC check: favour complete original wooden cases, whose provenance is more credible
  • Bonded storage: delivering straight into a bonded warehouse defers duties and eases cash flow
  • Pre-sale estimate: check current market prices and set your own maximum bid

For Sellers

  • Seller's commission: a percentage fee is charged, usually negotiable for high-value wines
  • Reserve protection: set a reserve price; the lot does not sell below it
  • Timing: demand is usually stronger when wines enter their drinking window or during the main auction seasons
  • Documents: complete purchase receipts and storage records increase buyer confidence
  • Lots: complete original cases of 6 or 12 bottles are usually more popular than single bottles
slides.7.title: Tax, Law and Cross-Border Compliance
slides.7.content:
Buying and selling wine across borders involves tax and legal issues; the rules differ greatly between markets and change over time, so check the latest official rules or consult a professional first.

🏦 Bonded Warehouses and Deferred Tax

How a bonded warehouse works: while wine is stored in a government-supervised bonded warehouse, import duty and VAT are not yet due; the tax obligation is triggered only when the wine is "released from bond"
In practice: professional bonded warehouses in places such as the UK and Hong Kong let wine change hands without physically moving, lowering cross-border costs
Costs and insurance: bonded warehouses charge storage per case, usually including insurance, and complete storage records are trusted more by auction houses

📋 Taiwan's Regulations

Import duties and taxes: imported wine is subject to customs duty, tobacco and alcohol tax calculated on alcohol content, and business tax; actual rates and calculations should follow the latest rules of the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance
Personal allowance: there is a duty-free limit on alcohol carried into Taiwan, beyond which it must be declared and taxed; large quantities must go through a licensed importer
Reselling a collection: the tax treatment of reselling wines after long-term collecting is complex, so consulting a professional accountant is advised

⚖️ Authentication and Disputes

Verifying authenticity: in a dispute, check batch numbers and release records with the estate, or engage a professional wine authenticator
Legal liability for counterfeits: selling counterfeit DOCG wine is illegal in Italy and the EU; in Taiwan it falls under rules such as the Tobacco and Alcohol Administration Act and the Trademark Act
Insurance: for valuable cellars, consider specialist wine insurance covering theft, fire, flood and transit damage
slides.8.title: Key Takeaways
slides.8.points.0: Italy exports more than €7 billion of wine a year, with the US accounting for about a quarter — the largest single export market
slides.8.points.1: Hong Kong became Asia's auction hub after abolishing wine import duty in 2008, and Asian high-net-worth collectors drive demand for top DOCGs
slides.8.points.2: The three leading auction houses: Christie's (London/New York), Sotheby's (worldwide, including Hong Kong), Hart Davis Hart (Chicago)
slides.8.points.3: Taiwan: wine education is widespread and enthusiasts take a deep interest in Barolo / Brunello / Amarone, collecting mainly to learn
slides.8.points.4: Japan: top-class sommeliers and a focus on food pairing, favouring elegant whites (Soave, Friulano) and refined reds
slides.8.points.5: The four digital tools: Wine-Searcher (prices), Vivino (community ratings), Liv-ex (trade exchange), Winebid (online auctions)
slides.8.points.6: Liv-ex indices are important indicators of overall fine-wine market trends, but past performance does not predict the future
slides.8.points.7: Bonded warehouses defer duty and VAT, and their storage records are trusted more by auction houses
slides.8.points.8: Duties and regulations for cross-border trade change, so follow the latest official rules (in Taiwan, the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance)
slides.8.points.9: For valuable cellars, consider specialist wine insurance covering theft, fire, flood and transit damage

slides.9.questions.4.question: What does OWC mean in wine auctions, and why does it matter?
slides.9.questions.4.options.1: Original Wooden Case — its provenance is more credible
slides.9.questions.4.explanation: OWC (Original Wooden Case) is the wooden case in which the estate ships the wine; a complete OWC suggests the wine is less likely to have been opened and split up and that its provenance is credible, so such lots are preferred at auction.
slides.9.questions.5.question: When importing wine into Taiwan, which of these is NOT a tax to consider?
slides.9.questions.5.options.1: Tobacco and alcohol tax based on alcohol content
slides.9.questions.5.explanation: Imported wine is subject to customs duty, tobacco and alcohol tax calculated on alcohol content, and business tax; vineyard land tax has nothing to do with importing. Actual rates should follow the latest rules of the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance.
